properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/15/2023 to LEATHERWOOD LLC in Morris Township, Greene county. 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: LEATHERWOOD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/15/2023
Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 8168595
Permit API: 059-24992
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/15/2023
Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Report Details

Violation ID: 864092
Permit API: 117-20309
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Gaines Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-10-02
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a FUI inspection at the Tilden Marcellus LLC - Pierson 801 located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 10/2/2019 @0845 hours. The weather was sunny 74 degrees. Onsite for the inspection was myself, Korey Starkey, DEP WQS; Jennifer Compton and Nathan Smelser, Tilden Marcellus; Farmer Boy Restoration; Civil and Environmental Consultants, Inc.(CEC) As of today's inspection, a large stain was observed on the gravel surface adjacent to the failed dump line measuring ~8'x4'(See Photo#1). Tilden's earthmoving sub-contractor, Farmer Boy Restoration, had used a small excavator to scrape the surface of the impacted pad area, fill slope (see photo #2) and dig a sump in the fill slope approximately 4' wide and 5' deep. Fluid that had accumulated in the bottom of the sump had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm(See Photo#3). Sample 4427-192 was collected from the fluid in the fill slope sump and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for SAC 942 analysis. CEC consultants had delineated the extent of the impacted area with white flags. The excavator, and CEC, were currently working to remove soil with an elevated conductivity in an area below the toe of the fill slope(See Photo#4,5). The excavated sump was then expanded across the fill slope. A wet gravel layer was observed ~3' below the pad surface that appeared to be the source of the >19.99mS/cm fluid entering the sump(See Photo#6). Jennifer Compton and CEC continued to screen the fill slope area and remove additional material. The impacted material was being staged on the pad surface, on the interior of the gas line, awaiting the delivery of more disposal boxes. Ms. Compton was also awaiting the delivery of a super sucker truck to remove additional pad material. Tilden Marcellus and CEC were advised to contact the DEP Environment Cleanups and Brownfields (ECB) Program to facilitate cleanup activities going forward. Violations cited previously in inspection report#2939891, dated 9/30/2019 are cited as OUTSTANDING against the 2H well, API#117-20309 at this time. We departed the site @1200 hours.

Violation ID: 8235148
Permit API: 015-23440
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Broadleaf Holdings" Marcellus well site. Tory Rogers called the DEP on Friday morning May 23, 2025 to report a release of approximately 9 gallons of diesel based drilling mud released from a flare stack to the pad surface that morning. I met with Tory Rogers, Jim Brown, Megan DePue (all 3 Repsol), and Scotty Brown (DEP, OGI) on site. While drilling a future Marcellus Shale well there was a control issue, so they lit the flare stack to burn off natural gas incurred. Some drilling mud blew out of the flare stack, estimated at 7 gallons onto pad containment, and 9 gallons on the pad surface. Rogers showed us where the flare stack released drilling mud. Resource Environmental directed excavation to remove pad material the drilling mud impacted, which was approximately a 10'X60' area. They completed the cleanup around 1600 hrs the same day the release occurred. The material is in 2 dumpsters on the NE corner of the pad. I got a 1.5 ppm reading with a 10.6 eV MiniRae photoionization detector (PID) from the removed pad material, and a 0.0 ppm PID reading from the remediated pad surface, which indicates the cleanup sufficiently removed the impacted pad material. Drill cuttings in a dumpster near the drill rig gave a 135.7 ppm reading. Violations cited to the 015-23893 drilling permit are considered immediately corrected.Rogers explained they increased the density of the drill mud from 12.8 lbs/gal to 13.5 lbs/gal to provide more well control.Repsol laid the containment on this pad on February 26 thru March 3, 2025. Felt liner (130 mil thickness) went down first, then wood/steel mats. Fine gravel is used to fill gaps between the mats.Precision Drilling 110 started drilling 4 new Marcellus wells at this site on April 1 2025, and expect to finish drilling around June 10, 2025. There are also 4 existing Marcellus wells here. They drill on water based mud for the vertical section, then switch to diesel based mud for the kickoff (curve) and horizontal section.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity (EC) of 0.68-1.7 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.62FJLP

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. An onsite meeting was scheduled with Petro Erie Inc. and the Department which developed this Inspection Report.Individuals present at the onsite meeting:Harry Rhoades -Owner/Operator of Petro Erie Inc.Chris Rhoades -Driver for Harry RhoadesRob Bechtel -PA DEPRick Willey -PA DEPAlan Wolf -PA DEPLucas Eichner -PA DEPSteve Wells -PA DEPThe meeting was started off by Rob Bechtel stating the reason for the meeting and what was discovered during a previous site inspection on 7/21/2023 with violations cited. It was discussed that there is a potential that the discharge of produced fluid from the tank battery may have impacted the Reno, PA public water supply. Mr. Rhoades asked if the pubic water supply was now safe to drink and if regular testing was being conducted. We informed him that the oil and gas program was collecting samples for analysis to determine if the water supply was impacted by oil and gas activity and that the Safe Drinking Water program was working with Venango Water Company related to the public water supply. The discussion with Mr. Rhoades made him aware of the fact that there are more than several concerns with his lease. The Department recommended that he hire an environmental consultant to help him through the cleanup and reporting process of an Act 2 cleanup regarding the discharge of produced fluid and the potential impact of the Reno public water supply. Other violations were discussed regarding the other wells on his lease. Statements that were made by Mr. Rhoades during the meeting:-He is the only owner/operator of Petro Erie Inc-He pumps the wells on the lease himself-One well on the lease is on a timer and pumps when he is not present-Mr. Rhoades does not know what occurred at the site referring to the discharge of produced fluid-Wants the water of the households in Reno tested-Hauled 3 loads of brine, 1 load hauled by Gavin to disposal in OH and 2 loads hauled by Paul Weaver to a frac job in West Virginia-Stated that the tank battery and the impact area was present when he purchased the lease

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 986954
Permit API: 081-21907
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/03/2023
Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the Salt Run HC EXT Pad A location. Inspection accompanied by EQT Company Man Matt Casler and EQT Senior EHS Coordinator Zac Subra. Weather conditions at time of inspection are overcast and 38 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while the spill response is ongoing.According to the Emergency Response Notification Report submitted by EHS supervisor Rick Hall, 'approximately one barrel of production fluid was released to the pad surface off containment and approximately 50 barrels of production fluid were released on containment at the Salt Run Pad A Extension. EQT was in the middle of a frac on the pad when a pipe came apart and spilled the production fluid onto containment and soil. Tobias Machining and Welding was contracted to perform remediation worm on the impacted soils. No waterways or stormwater structures were impacted.'During site inspection and discussions with Mr. Subra and Mr. Casler, the following details were reported. Universal Pressure Pumping was conducting a zipper frac of four wells at the time of the incident. At around 2:19 AM, while fracturing stage 11 of the 11H well (API #081-21907) the high pressure iron pipe connecting the frac missile to the well head failed resulting in a high pressure release of production fluid and frac sand. The fluid pressure at the time of the incident was 9,450 PSI and the pumping volume was 90 barrels per minute of the slurry mixture. The fluid release was brought under control in 20 seconds. Due to the pressure of the release, the slurry mixture of sand and fluid sprayed vertically into the air with a majority landing in secondary containment while an unknown volume landed on the pad rock surface along the south side of the pad. The affected area outside containment is an L-shaped section along the south access way approximately 200' by 15' with another area of 50 by' 50' affected adjacent to the Modular Aboveground Storage Structure (Photos 3,6 and 7). At time of inspection, Matt Tusing with Penn E and R is delineating the edges of the affected pad surface. A skidsteer is scraping affected pad material and placing it into a lined steel rolloff container. According to Mr. Subra, three rolloffs are reserved for pad rock material, each capable of holding 18 tons of material. Scraped pad rock will be staged in the lined containers at the Salt Run Pad B location pending analysis. Two vac trucks are on site to vacuum production fluid from the containment surface. A pressure washing crew is en route to clean fluid and sand from the secondary containment structure. Due to the volume of fluid which was released from the failed high pressure fitting and the unknown volume of fluid released to the pad surface, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Mr. Subra indicated that Act 2 remediation will be undertaken by EQT. Violations noted.

An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).All standing water observed on the pad surface was frozen solid.There are 2 recently completed wells onsite and their American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers are posted at the site entrance; I was unable to confirm if the wells were tagged due to them currently being covered (photos #1 and 2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the containment structure did not contain any standing water. The tanks were labeled as per the Department's request (photos #5 and 6). A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and held in secondary containment (photo #7).Numerous upright brine tanks and temporary storage tanks are still noted onsite and held in their respective secondary containment structures which appear to be functioning as intended (photos #8 and 9). Multiple lined and covered residual waste containers are in use onsite for ongoing Act 2 remediation efforts as well as disassembly of the pad wide containment system (rig matting) and tear down of completions equipment (photos #10 and 11). No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #17). The basin inlet remains shut in and no fluids or diesel sheen was observed (photo #18). Soil in the basin field measured for EC at ~0.72mS/cm (photo #19).Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Comments: On 12/21/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Spesak F41 well site following violations issued on 11/16/2023 (IR 3647660, Enforcement 422104). I was accompanied by David Blaker of Diversified. Violations of 78.66(b), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), and 91.34(a) were issued on 11/16/2023 for the release of production fluid to the ground within the tank battery. The tanks within the battery that previously displayed elevated conductivity readings below the lower valves were tanks 1-3. Readings obtained on 11/16/2023 displayed results of Over range - range up to 20.00 m/S (tank 1), 16.65 m/S (tank 2), and 10.55 m/S (tank 3).The following was observed during inspection on 12/21/2023:The area under each valve appeared as though soils were removed - no buckets of contaminated material were noted on site. The readings obtained during inspection were as follows: 1.14 m/S and 0.28 m/S (tank 1), 18.14 m/S and 12.52 m/S (tank 2), and 1.53 m/S and 1.45 m/S (tank 3) (Photos 1-9). At the valve of tank 2, there appeared to be a sound like fluid/air bubbles escaping. I communicated this to the operator while onsite. Due to the observed elevated conductivity readings under tank 2, the violations of 78.66(b), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Comments: On January 29, 2021, Don Stevenson of Beech Resources reported a spill of brine water to the DEP. The DEP spoke with Mr. Stevenson on February 1, 2021 to follow up with the reported spill. Beech Resources was in the process of pulling up their liner used for the recent stimulation of the new wells drilled and noticed staining on the pad surface. Mr. Stevenson estimated the volume of the spill to be about 1,500 gallons. The area of impact that was excavated is reported to be 100 ft. by 125 ft. and about 6 inches of the pad surface was removed. When DEP spoke with Mr. Stevenson on the phone, Beech Resources had finished excavating the impacted soil on Saturday January 30, 2021, and Penn E&R had collected confirmatory samples for the site. DEP was unable to complete an in person investigation due to the winter weather. DEP will follow up with a site inspection as soon as weather allows. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Report No. 3139277.

Comments: Met with Diversified supervisor Mark McCracken on 9/6/24 at the brine spill that Diversified reported on 9/5/24 for well 033-23855. According to Mr. McCracken a small stone punctured the bottom of the brine tank causing the release. Upon arriving onsite I observed where the release happened. I observed an excavated area approximately 35' long by 15' wide. Most of the main release occurred directly underneath where the tank was sitting. The brine tank has been disconnected and emptied. I screened the excavated areas using a soil probe. A few spots still have some elevated readings 1.15 mS/cm and 2.25 mS/cm. Those areas have been marked by the operator. The operator plans to remove the rest of the impacted soils on Monday. Two tri-axle loads of soils have already been removed from the site. In addition, I screened outside the delineated area. No other elevated areas were observed. For now, the hole has been covered in plastic. The operator will be using Act 2 for site remediation. A crew later today will be coming to install E and S controls around the perimeter of the spill. Violations have been cited.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/12/2022
Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 955505
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/12/2022
Comments: On May 12, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The small berm that was built to collect the seep was was dry and any water that is collected in that area is being vacuumed out. Upon arrival at the well pad, STL Resources was vacuuming water out of the northwest stormwater vault. The conductivity of the water that could not be vacuumed out was 2,500 uS/cm. About 18 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in this vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. STL Resources has back filled and rebuilt the excavated southwest and northwest infiltration berms that were impacted by the spill. DEP screened the water that had pooled up behind the northwest infiltration for conductivity and that resulted in 187 uS/cm. The conductivity of the small amount of water that pooled up behind the southwest infiltration berm was 40 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.1 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 188 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 196.2 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 59.9 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 44.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 133.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. During the inspection, STL Resources consultants were collecting soil samples from the well pad in a grid like pattern to delineate the area of the production fluid spill. Two of the holes that remained open had water pooled in them. Test Pit-209 which was about 7 yards to the north of the northwest stormwater vault had water pooled in it. The conductivity of the water in test pit-209 was 2030 uS/cm and soil conductivity was difficult to measure to due the looseness of the soil in the hole. Soil sample 0651-117 was collected from this test pit and will be analyzed for the Bureau of Labs SAC 530. Test Pit 211 which was about 15 yards to the north of 035-21325, had water pooled in it. The conductivity of the water was 3,800 uS/cm and the soil conductivity was 1,180 uS/cm. Soil Sample 0651-118 was collected from this test pit and will be analyzed for the Bureau of Labs SAC 530. DEP spoke with STL Resources Seth Rodriguez and he said that STL Resources is planning to hydroseed the site's earthen infiltration berms and parts of the site that are lacking vegetation. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 5, 6, and 8 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a ROUTINE inspection of the Seneca Resources - Cruttenden 846 Well Site located in MIddlebury Twp, Tioga Co. on 11/9/22 @1400 hours. The weather was 46 degrees, partly sunny, winds WNW @14mph. Activity onsite consists of flowback and production of the recently completed 30HU-34HU, 39HU and 78H wells.Sections of the pad-wide secondary containment and rig mats have been removed. The pad material in these areas appears to have been removed lowering the surface of the pad by approximately 10-18" in comparison to the surrounding areas. Puddles on the pad surface had field measured conductivity of 0.99mS/cm to 6.35mS/cm in some areas (please see attached photos for locations of conductivity readings). Sample 4427-295 was collected from the puddle with a field measured conductivity of 2.99mS/cm - 6.35mS/cm west of the well heads. Sample 4427-298 was collected from a puddle, in a scraped down area, on the east side of the well heads with a field measured conductivity of 9.6mS/cm. Soil sample 4427-296 was collected from the edge of the remaining pad material under secondary containment. Soil sample 4427-297 was collected from the south edge of the well pad. Onsite personnel were notified of my findings. It is recommended a vac truck be dispatched to removed accumulated fluid from secondary containment and puddles from the pad surface.A violation of CSL 402(b) is cited against the 34HU well API#117-22129 at this time due. Violations of SWMA 301, 25 Pa Code 78a.57(a) are pending the results of samples 4427-295, 296,297 and 298. I departed the site at 1540 hours.

Comments: On April 30, 2026, the Department conducted Routine Complete Inspection of Diversified's Thompson/Bloniarz 1 plugged well located in Georges Township, Fayette County following IR 4167430, where violations were issued for failure to have a site restoration plan on site. Refer to IR 4190461 for the closure of these violations.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on March 7, 2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/07/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 12/07/2025 and a well site restoration report should be submitted to the Department by 2/05/2026. Refer to IR 4190445, for the status of the COA.At the time of this inspection, a site restoration plan was observed to be present in an on-site mailbox. Erosion and sedimentation controls were observed to be removed from the plugged gas well site despite the site not being permanently stabilized. According to the E and S plan on-site CFS is to be installed along the perimeter of the site. Although no active erosion and sedimentation issues were observed at this time, there is the potential for future erosion and sedimentation issues to occur.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued at this time for failure to have E and S controls installed on site until the site is permanently stabilized.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/28/2024 to JKLM ENERGY LLC in Summit Township, Potter county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: JKLM ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/28/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8181244
Permit API: 105-21857
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Summit Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/28/2024
Comments: On 03/28/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an inspection of JKLM Energy LLC's Sweden Valley 101 multi-well pad located in Summit Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1150 hours, weather was 40F and partly cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).There was standing water on the pad surface which field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of approximately 199 - 226us/cm.There are 3 wells tagged with American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers and capable of producing and located onsite (photos #2 and 3). 3 gas processing units (GPUs) stationed in a secondary containment structure are also located onsite (photo #4). The GPU containment structure contained greater than 10% standing water which field measured for EC at ~136.6us/cm. There is evidence of damage to the GPU secondary containment structure (photos #5 and 6). There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #7); the containment structure contained standing water which field measured for EC at ~10.1 us/cm. The brine pump secondary containment structure contained water which field measured for EC at ~13.66mS/cm (photos #8 and 9).A dehydrator is located onsite and associated chemicals are stationed in secondary containment (photo #10). A compressor unit and compressor waste fluids tank is located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #11). Water in the compressor fluids unit had a visible sheen and field measured for EC at ~36.6us/cm; the containment lining shows signs of damage (photos #12 and 13). The compressor waste oil storage tank is stationed in secondary containment and holding water with a sheen on it (photos #14 and 15). Oil was noted leaking from the compressor oil tank pipe fittings and staining was visible on the ground (photos #16 - 18). The affected area was approximately 10ft x 2ft, I excavated approximately 6in deep and still noted staining (photo #18). I contacted a representative from JKLM who notified the DEP spill reporting hotline of the incident and dispatched personnel to excavate and remediate the affected area immediately. Please see attached file regarding cleanup and remediation. Areas surrounding the well pad remain permanently stabilized with vegetative cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. 2 infiltration basins serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls (photos #19 and 20). The PCSM controls appear to be permanently stabilized and functioning as intended.The DEP recommends the following:-Properly disposing of water in all secondary containment structures to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e) and 25 PA 78a64a(f).-Repairing all damaged secondary containment structures to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(d).Due to the release of ~5-10 gallons of compressor unit oil, the following violations are cited against API #: 105-21857 and noted as immediately corrected based on JKLM Energy LLC's immediate remediation efforts.-CSL 402(b)-SWMA 301I departed the site at 1350 hours.
